content.title: About
content.content: Soy nuts are roasted soybeans (Glycine max) that have a light nutty flavor and a crunchy texture. They are often used as an alternative snack for people avoiding traditional tree nuts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Soy nuts are made from soybeans, one of the most widely cultivated legume crops worldwide.
Unlike most nuts, soy nuts are not true nuts botanically; they are seeds of a legume.
In Asian cuisine, especially Japanese, boiled soybeans in the pod are called edamame, a close relative to roasted soy nuts.
Soy is rich in isoflavones, which can have phytoestrogenic effects.
Roasting enhances aroma but can also reduce some heat‑sensitive vitamins.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Soy nuts contain about 35 % protein, making them an excellent source of plant‑based protein.

items.title: Contains healthy fats
items.content: They provide polyunsaturated fatty acids, including omega‑6 and a modest amount of omega‑3.

items.title: Source of B vitamins
items.content: Soy nuts supply B‑vitamins such as thiamine, riboflavin, and folate, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Rich in minerals
items.content: They contain iron, magnesium, phosphorus, and calcium, supporting bone health and nerve function.

items.title: Phytoestrogens
items.content: Soy isoflavones may help balance hormones, especially for women during menopause.

items.title: Soy allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to soy products.

items.title: Phytic acid content
items.content: Phytic acid can reduce the absorption of certain minerals when consumed in large amounts.

items.title: Genetically modified organisms (GMOs)
items.content: Most soy worldwide is GMO; choose certified organic varieties if you wish to avoid GMOs.

items.title: High sodium in salted versions
items.content: Salted soy nuts can contain a lot of sodium, which is undesirable for people with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Soy nuts can be eaten straight as a snack, tossed into salads, soups, rice or noodle dishes, and used in vegetarian and vegan recipes as a nut substitute.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store soy nuts in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent the fats from becoming rancid.
